back_translation: Woe to you, O destroyer who has never been destroyed! O traitor whom no one has ever betrayed! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; when you have betrayed to the utmost, they will betray you.
O LORD, have mercy on us! We wait for You. Be the strength of their arm every morning, and our salvation in time of distress.
At the thundering of Your majestic voice the peoples flee; when You arise, the nations scatter.
Your plunder will be gathered up as the young locust gathers; like a swarm of locusts pouncing, men pounce upon it.
The LORD is exalted on high, for He dwells above; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
He will be the sure foundation of your times, a rich storehouse of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of the LORD is Zion's treasure.
Behold, their brave men cry out in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
The highways are deserted; travelers have vanished. The treaty has been torn up and violated, the witnesses are despised, and human life is counted as worthless.
The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and withered. Sharon has become like the desert Arabah; Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves until bare.
"Now I will arise," says the LORD. "Now I will be exalted on high; now I will be lifted up in honor.
You conceive chaff and give birth to stubble; your own breath is a fire that will consume you.
The peoples will be burned as limestone is burned to lime, like thorns cut down and set on fire.
You who are far away, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge My mighty power."
The sinners in Zion are terrified; trembling seizes the ungodly: "Who among us can dwell with the consuming fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting flames?"

He who walks in righteousness and speaks what is upright, who rejects profit from extortion and oppression, who shakes his hands free of accepting bribes, who stops his ears from hearing plots of bloodshed, and shuts his eyes tight against looking upon evil —
that one will dwell on the heights; a towering rock fortress will be his refuge; his bread will be given him, and his water will be sure and unfailing.
Your eyes will see the King in His beauty, and will behold a land stretching far and wide.
Your heart will look back on the terror of those days: "Where is the one who counted and recorded? Where is the one who weighed? Where is the one who counted the towers?"
You will no longer see that insolent people, a people whose language is too deep to make out, who stammer in a tongue you cannot understand.

Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed festivals! Your eyes will see Jerusalem as a peaceful dwelling, a tent that will not be moved; its stakes will never be pulled up, and not one of its cords will be snapped.
For there the LORD in His majesty will be for us like broad rivers and wide canals, where no galley with oars will travel and no stately ship will pass.
For the LORD is our Judge; the LORD is our Lawgiver; the LORD is our King. He Himself will save us.
Your ship's rigging hangs slack; it cannot hold the mast firm in its place, nor can the sail be spread. Then abundant spoils will be divided; even the lame will carry off plunder.
And no resident will say, "I am sick"; the people who dwell there will be forgiven of their iniquity.
